title: Aging and surface renewal permit fixed oxygen use in the central P02 oxygen loss from 2013 to 2022
abstract: We link repeated North Pacific tracer age distributions by aging and surface renewal. We reuse published P02 regional CFC-12, SF6 and oxygen means. At density 26.5 and 180-160 W, AOU rose 8.499 micromol/kg in 2013-2022. With fixed oxygen use of 4 micromol/kg/year, a source budget of 300 micromol/kg and 5 percent tracer tolerance, the minimum final fraction ventilated after 2013 is 13.241 percent with age-selective removal. Equal survival at every initial age permits 18.903-20.342 percent. An exact survivor-measure linear program removes the unknown survival-probability product. Positive witnesses and independent reconstruction checks support the bounds. Equal-survival fits occur at tested rates 3.7-4.6, but none at 2 percent tolerance. A 100 micromol/kg component oxygen floor removes all 5 percent fits in the tested rate profile. Three-degree binning retains the main result. These are conditional compatibility bounds, not measured circulation or an outcrop attribution. Surface-only input, fixed source saturation, uniform oxygen use and free renewal histories limit inference.

display.caption: Conditional replacement bounds and finite oxygen-use rate profiles for temporally linked P02 spectra.

citations.reason: Exact regional aggregate inputs and prior unlinked fixed-use test.
